items.title: Mississauga pulls plug on big new data centres for 1 year
items.summary: 20-plus residents showed up to oppose a proposed data centre — now Mississauga has a city-wide one-year freeze. Council unanimously approved the one-year pause on all new digital infrastructure with a total peak power demand of 10 megawatts or greater. Mississauga city council has passed a one-year moratorium on new major data centres while staff study environmental, land-use and infrastructural impacts. The temporary interim control bylaw was approved at the Sept. 16 council meeting and applies to all citywide facilities with a peak power demand of 10 megawatts or greater. While existing and already approved digital facilities will continue to operate, they cannot expand their operations if it pushes their peak demand to 10 megawatts or more. Facilities requiring under 10 megawatts are exempt from this ban, according to the bylaw document. According to the document, digital infrastructure includes any building or part of it that contains computer systems, servers and components used to store or process digital information. The freeze has come into effect immediately as staff review zoning rules, assess operational impacts including water use, heat generation, noise, backup power emissions and grid capacity concerns.

items.title: Ticket holders still wait for answers after Mississauga comedy festival ‘postponed’
items.summary: The Great Outdoors Comedy Festival was supposed to bring three days of major comedy acts to Mississauga’s Erindale Park last weekend, but the event was postponed just days before it was scheduled to begin and ticket holders are still waiting for a clearer explanation of what happened. The festival was scheduled for Sept. 11 to 13, with John Mulaney, Hasan Minhaj, Ronny Chieng and several other comedians among the performers announced for the inaugural Mississauga event. Instead, organizers announced on Sept. 8 the festival would not go ahead as planned. The City of Mississauga says the decision was made by festival organizers and that the municipality has no additional information about why the event was postponed. “The Great Outdoors Comedy Festival decided to postpone this weekend’s event in Mississauga. com. “The city will continue to work with the festival organizers on next steps. com reached out to festival organizers twice for more information about the decision, including questions about the reason for the postponement, a potential new date and the status of ticket refunds, but did not receive a response. The city’s response also suggests the decision was not made by the municipality, despite the significant preparations that had already been made for the event at Erindale Park. Mississauga had announced temporary park restrictions beginning Sept. 6 and continuing through Sept. 16 to allow for event setup, operations and teardown.

items.title: Massive street food festival returns to Mississauga’s Cooksville
items.summary: One of Mississauga’s biggest food festivals is even bigger this year, with nearly 100 vendors and extended hours. Taste of Cooksville, organized by the Cooksville Business Improvement Area is back on Sept. 19 and 20 for a weekend of delicious food, live music, family entertainment, and more in the historic Cooksville neighbourhood. Like previous years, the festival is free for everyone to attend. There’s even more time to enjoy the food and festivities with extended hours, running from 11 am to 11 pm on Saturday, Sept. 19 and 11 am to 8 pm on Sunday, Sept. 20. Nearly one hundred vendors and food trucks will be lined up along 47 Dundas St W near Hurontario, offering sweet and savoury cuisine from around the world. There’ll be a ton of variety, making it easy to turn a trip to the festival into a full afternoon or evening of eating and exploring. Pair your food with a refreshingly cold drink from the beer garden, presented by Port Credit’s Old Credit Brewing Co. While trying some delicious eats, enjoy nonstop live music and performances on the main stage, bouncy inflatables, workshops and activities for the kids, and a brand-new car show putting an exciting lineup of vehicles on display. More info on vendors and entertainment will be posted soon on the event’s website. Taste of Cooksville is one of the city’s most popular yearly events since 2019, and is now among the biggest food festivals in the GTA.

items.title: Charges dropped against Mississauga jeweller accused in $24-million Pearson gold heist
items.summary: Virtually all of the loot remains unaccounted for after the brazen gold-and-cash theft at Toronto’s Pearson International Airport on April 17, 2023. Ali Raza a jeweller from Mississauga had all charges against him, related to the 2023 Pearson Gold Heist, dropped in a court hearing Wednesday. Pictured with council Brij Mohan. Mississauga jeweller Ali Raza blinked away tears but said he was happy outside the Brampton courthouse on Wednesday, minutes after hearing he is no longer facing a charge of receiving stolen gold from the largest gold heist in Canadian history. He had been charged with knowingly receiving large amounts of gold stolen in a massive heist at Toronto’s Pearson airport on April 17, 2023. “Ali’s life was destroyed,” his lawyer Brij Mohan said, standing close to his client. “His family life was destroyed. ” “I am innocent,” Raza, 37, said, his eyes watering. ” In a brief court hearing Wednesday, Crown attorney Jelena Vlacic said they made the decision to stop the proceedings against Raza based on new evidence. Vlacic said that evidence is covered under a publication ban and cannot be reported at this time.

items.title: Mississauga approves temporary pause for large-scale data centre development
items.summary: The pause will give the City time to conduct a comprehensive review of the sector. Today, City Council approved an Interim Control By-law (ICBL) that temporarily prohibits the development of major digital infrastructure facilities such as data centres for up to one year. An ICBL is a provincial planning tool that allows a municipality to temporarily pause a specific type of development in a defined area for further study. This gives municipalities time to determine the best long-term planning approach before new development proceeds. The ICBL approved today applies to applications for new major digital infrastructure facilities, including conversions or expansions of existing facilities, located across the City (as shown in this map). These large-scale facilities have computer systems, servers and related equipment that store or process digital information. Under the ICBL, facilities that have a total peak power demand of 10 megawatts or more will not be permitted for up to one year. During the temporary pause, the City is conducting a comprehensive policy review for major digital infrastructure facilities. The review will assess whether policies and regulations, such as the Official Plan and Zoning By-law, need to be updated. It will also consider any new guidance or requirements from the province’s Data Centre Playbook as they become available. There will be opportunities for public engagement during the review. An interim report outlining the study scope and timeline will be presented to Council later this year. Updates will be posted on the City’s data centre policy review webpage. Once the review is complete, City staff will bring recommendations to Council to help guide future planning policies and regulations for data centres and other major digital infrastructure projects.
